To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ROA of a controlled nonlinear polynomial system can be computed via a convex hierarchy of LPs over the space of probability measures, and that the hierarchy is converging in a sense that we make precise.

(1) the ROA can always be computed via convex LPs over the space of system trajectories; (2) these LPs can be solved approximately by solving a hierarchy of convex LMIs with asymptotically decreasing conservatism; (3) the dual LP can be solved by a sequence of Lasserre's sum-of-squares hierarchies; and (4) the resulting semialgebraic sets are outer approximations of increasing precision of the ROA.
the convex computation of the region-of-attraction of a controlled polynomial system can be achieved by solving a convex LP problem and approximated via convex LMI hierarchies.

the following three problems: 1) the problem of computing an upper bound for the region of attraction; 2) the problem of finding a lower bound for the region; and 3) the problem of obtaining the exact region of attraction.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the ROA is convex, which allows us to solve the problem of computing it by solving a sequence of convex LPs.
convexity is a property of the primal problem of computing the set of trajectories that reach the target set, rather than a property of the dual Lyapunvov conditions.
convexity of ROA computation is a direct consequence of convexity of the underlying LP problem and that this convexity is not an artefact of the dual Lyapunovo approach.
